scenario: 题目要求 validate、match、find、extract 或 classify 某种文本格式。
scenario_en: The prompt asks you to validate, match, find, extract, or classify some text format.
q: 这通常说明你进入了哪类模式？
q_en: What pattern does this usually point to?
options: 最短路径
字符串匹配与解析
LRU 缓存
Union-Find
options_en: Shortest path
String matching and parsing
LRU cache
Union-Find (disjoint set)
why: 这些动词都指向文本处理，但还要继续判断是固定模式、多个模式、格式验证还是字段抽取。字符串题的关键是工具选择和分层。
why_en: Validate, match, find, extract, and classify are strong cues for a string matching or parsing problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果文本只是作为节点标签而问题问依赖顺序或路径，图算法可能才是核心；不要只因有字符串就套字符串模式。
tradeoff: 识别字符串工具箱 vs 被无关算法名带偏

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略：优先淘汰最久未被访问的缓存条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU, or Least Recently Used, evicts the cache entry that has gone longest without being accessed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并查集：支持合并两个集合、查询两个元素是否属于同一集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Union-Find, or Disjoint Set Union, supports merging sets and checking whether two elements are in the same set.

optionExplanations: 最短路径答的是图上两点间最省代价的路线；除非文本只是节点标签、真正问的是依赖顺序，否则这几个动词跟路径没关系。
对，validate/match/find/extract/classify 这类动词就是在喊字符串匹配与解析，先认出工具箱再挑具体工具。
LRU 管的是缓存该淘汰谁，靠访问顺序判断，跟判断文本是不是某种格式完全是两件事。
Union-Find 用来合并集合、查两个元素是不是同一组，题面这几个动词不涉及合并关系，所以用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Shortest path finds the cheapest route between two graph nodes; unless the text is just a node label and you're really asking about dependency order, these verbs have nothing to do with paths.
Right — those five cue words in the prompt (checking, matching, searching, pulling out data, or labeling text) point straight at string work, not graphs or caches.
LRU decides which cache entry to evict based on access order, a different question from recognizing a text format.
Union-Find merges sets and checks shared membership; none of these verbs involve merging anything, so it doesn't apply.

q: 哪些题面信号常指向字符串匹配/解析？
q_en: Which prompt signals often point to string matching or parsing?
options: 输入格式通过例子给出，例如日志行或 IP
需要从一行文本中提取字段
需要 against 固定词表或 schema 校验
只问无权图最短路径
options_en: The input format is given by example, like a log line or an IP.
You need to extract fields from a single line of text.
You need to check input against a fixed vocabulary or schema.
The problem only asks for shortest path in an unweighted graph.
why: 格式样例、字段抽取和固定词表都是文本结构问题。无权最短路径属于图搜索。
why_en: Example-based formats, field extraction, and fixed vocabularies are common string-parsing signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先定义好的数据结构或字段规则，用来校验输入是否合法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is a predefined structure or set of field rules used to validate input.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用已匹配前缀信息跳过重复比较的字符串匹配算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KMP, the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm, uses a partial-match table to skip redundant comparisons during search.

optionExplanations: 对，例子给出格式说明你要写一个通用匹配器而不是记住一个具体值，这就是字符串识别信号。
对，从一行里抠字段说明输入是平面结构，regex 或 split 是候选工具。
对，对固定词表或 schema 校验就是在判断成员关系，Trie 或哈希表是候选工具。
错，无权图最短路径是图搜索问题，跟文本格式识别没关系，别被字符串这个词带偏。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when the format comes from examples like a log line, you're building a general-purpose matcher, not memorizing one value.
Right — pulling fields out of one line means the input is flat, so regex or split become candidates.
Right — testing input against a known word list or schema is a membership check, so a trie or hash set fits.
Wrong — unweighted shortest path is a graph-search problem, unrelated to recognizing a text format.

q: 填空：四种子工具的典型适用场景。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: the best-fit scenarios for four string tools.
text: 找一个固定模式可先用{{暴力搜索}}；匹配很多固定模式用{{Trie}}；验证有阶段/模式的格式用{{有限状态机}}；从平面结构里抽字段用{{Regex}}。
why: 字符串题不是单一算法，而是工具箱。选错工具会导致过度设计或无法处理上下文。
why_en: The string toolkit maps single patterns to brute force, many fixed patterns to tries, modes to FSMs, and flat extraction to regex.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有限状态机：一组状态加上按输入字符触发的转移，只有落在接受状态才算合法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An FSM, or Finite State Machine, is a set of states with input-driven transitions that accepts only when it ends in an accepting state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用符号描述文本匹配规则的表达式，适合从平面结构中抽取字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A regex, or regular expression, describes text-matching rules and is well suited to extracting fields from flat structures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把字符串按共享前缀组织成树形结构的数据结构，用于快速匹配大量固定模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie organizes strings by shared character prefixes so many fixed patterns can be matched quickly.

scenario: 只需要在一段中等长度文本里找一个固定 pattern 出现的位置。
scenario_en: You only need to find where one fixed pattern appears in a medium-length text.
q: 合理的起点是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable starting point?
options: 先实现 Aho-Corasick 多模式匹配
先做拓扑排序再搜索
简单暴力滑窗搜索
维护两个堆求中位数
options_en: Implement Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching first
Run a topological sort before searching
A simple brute-force sliding-window search
Maintain two heaps to track a running median
why: 单个 pattern、规模不大时，暴力搜索短、可读、容易验证。先有正确 baseline，再考虑更快算法。
why_en: For one fixed pattern in moderate text, brute-force search is often the simplest correct baseline.
whenOtherWins: 如果 pattern 很多或文本巨大到 O(nm) 不够，应考虑 trie、KMP 或更专门的多模式算法。
tradeoff: 简单正确的 baseline vs 提前上重型多模式算法
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Text[Text] --> Window[Slide window]
  Pattern[Pattern] --> Compare[Compare chars]
  Window --> Compare
  Compare --> Match{Equal?}
  Match -->|yes| Return[Return index]
  Match -->|no| Shift[Shift one]

termDefinitions.meaning: 多模式字符串匹配算法，能在一次扫描中同时查找多个固定模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Aho-Corasick is a multi-pattern string-matching algorithm that finds many fixed patterns in a single scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每条边都从前面指向后面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from an earlier node to a later one.

optionExplanations: Aho-Corasick 是为同时找很多个模式预建的自动机，只有一个 pattern 时这套构建成本纯属浪费。
拓扑排序回答的是有向无环图里节点的先后顺序，跟在文本里找一个子串完全不是一回事。
对，只有一个固定 pattern、文本规模不大时，暴力滑窗最短最好读，也方便当后续优化的对照基准。
两个堆维护的是动态中位数这类排序统计量，答不出这个 pattern 出现在哪的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Aho-Corasick precompiles an automaton for many patterns at once; building that for a single pattern is pure overkill.
Topological sort answers node ordering in a DAG, a different question from locating a substring in text.
Right — when there's just one pattern and the text isn't huge, a plain window-and-compare scan is easy to write, read, and trust.
Two heaps track a running median-style statistic, which can't answer where this pattern shows up.

scenario: 面试官问暴力字符串搜索的最坏复杂度，想看你是否知道它何时会不够快。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks for the worst-case complexity of brute-force string search to see when it stops being fast enough.
q: 暴力字符串搜索的最坏时间复杂度是什么？
q_en: What is the worst-case time complexity of brute-force string search?
options: O(1)，与输入长度无关
O(log n)，二分类常见复杂度
O(V + E)，图遍历类复杂度
O(nm)，n 是文本长度、m 是模式长度
options_en: O(1), independent of input length
O(log n), common in binary-search style algorithms
O(V + E), common in graph-traversal algorithms
O(n times m), where n is text length and m is pattern length
why: 公式来自每个起点最坏要比较 m 个字符、共有约 n 个起点，n×m 就是后续判断“暴力是否够用”的依据：文本或模式一变大，就该考虑 trie/KMP。实际输入常因早期 mismatch 而更快。
why_en: Brute-force string search is O(n times m) in the worst case, though early mismatches make real interview inputs faster in practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大 O 记号，表示最坏情况下操作次数随 n 和 m 的乘积增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Big-O notation showing the worst-case operation count grows with the product of n and m.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图算法常见复杂度，V 是顶点数、E 是边数，如 BFS/拓扑排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A common graph-algorithm complexity where V is vertex count and E is edge count, as in BFS or topological sort.

scenario: 你在写一个函数，返回某个固定 pattern 在 text 里出现的所有起始下标。
scenario_en: You are writing a function that returns all start indexes where a fixed pattern appears in text.
q: 下面这段暴力字符串搜索代码的核心思路是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea in this brute-force string search code?
options: 按 pattern 长度滑动窗口逐一比较
构建最小堆维护候选起点
先做拓扑排序再扫描
维护 LRU 顺序淘汰旧匹配
options_en: Slide a pattern-length window and compare it at each position
Build a min-heap to track candidate start positions
Run a topological sort before scanning
Maintain LRU order to evict old matches
why: 它直接枚举每个可能起点，切片比较是否相等。可读性高，也适合当更快算法的参考 oracle。
why_en: This brute-force search slides a pattern-length window over every possible start position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在这里指“参考 oracle”：一个已知正确、可用来核对更快实现是否正确的简单版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference oracle is a known-correct, simple implementation used to check that a faster version behaves the same way.

optionExplanations: 对，代码里 for 循环枚举每个起点，切片比较跟 pattern 是否相等，就是逐位置滑窗比较。
堆是用来维护某种优先级顺序的，这段代码只有线性扫描加切片比较，没有需要排序的候选。
拓扑排序处理的是节点间的依赖顺序，这段代码里没有图、也没有依赖关系。
LRU 按访问顺序淘汰缓存条目，这段代码只是往 matches 里追加结果，没有淘汰逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the for loop enumerates every start index and slices a substring to compare against pattern, exactly a sliding window.
A heap tracks a priority ordering; this code is just a linear scan with slice comparisons, nothing to rank.
Topological sort orders dependent nodes; this code has no graph or dependency relationship at all.
LRU evicts by access order; this code only appends matches, no eviction logic here.

scenario: 你要判断输入是否属于一大批已知错误码、命令名或自动补全词表。
scenario_en: You need to check whether input belongs to a large known set of error codes, command names, or autocomplete terms.
q: 哪种结构最自然？
q_en: Which structure is the most natural fit?
options: Dijkstra 最短路径算法
Trie
双向链表实现的 LRU
对候选词做随机搜索
options_en: Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm
A trie
A doubly linked list backed LRU
Random search over the candidates
why: Trie 把固定词表编译成按字符共享前缀的结构。匹配时从根逐字符走，能高效处理许多固定模式。
why_en: A trie is the natural structure for matching or prefix-searching against many fixed strings.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一个固定模式，暴力或 KMP 更简单；如果需要复杂上下文或嵌套语法，Trie 不是完整解析器。
tradeoff: 预编译共享前缀 vs 逐个模式重复扫描
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Root[Root] --> C[c]
  C --> CA[a]
  CA --> CAT[t word]
  C --> CO[o]
  CO --> COT[t word]
  Root --> D[d]
  D --> DO[o]
  DO --> DOG[g word]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把字符串按共享前缀组织成树形结构的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie organizes strings by shared character prefixes in a tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在带权图中求单源最短路径的经典算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm computes single-source shortest paths in a weighted graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略：优先淘汰最久未被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU, or Least Recently Used, evicts the entry that has gone longest without being accessed.

optionExplanations: Dijkstra 求的是带权图里的最短路径，跟判断输入是不是属于一个固定词表没有关系。
对，Trie 把词表按共享前缀编译成树，从根逐字符走一遍就能判断成员关系，词表越大优势越明显。
双向链表加哈希表实现的是按访问顺序淘汰的缓存，答不出这个词在不在词表里。
对候选词做随机搜索既不可靠也没利用词表本身的前缀结构，规模一大就撑不住。
optionExplanations_en: Dijkstra finds shortest paths in a weighted graph, unrelated to checking whether input belongs to a fixed vocabulary.
Right — a trie compiles the vocabulary into a shared-prefix tree, so one walk from the root answers membership, and the win grows with vocabulary size.
A doubly linked list plus hash map builds an access-order cache, which can't answer 'is this word in the set'.
Randomly searching candidates is neither reliable nor uses the vocabulary's prefix structure, and it falls apart at scale.

q: 填空：Trie 查询的两个关键概念。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: two key ideas in trie lookup.
text: Trie 从{{根节点}}开始按字符走；到达带有{{is_end / terminal}} 标记的节点时，才表示完整单词匹配。
why: 只走到某个前缀节点不等于完整词命中。`starts_with` 和 `search` 的区别就在终止标记。
why_en: Trie search walks from the root and only a terminal marker confirms a complete word.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Root[Root] --> C[c]
C --> CA[ca]
CA --> CAT[cat end]
CA --> CAR[car end]
Root --> D[d]
D --> DOG[dog end]

termDefinitions.meaning: Trie 节点上的终止标记，为真表示从根到此节点的路径正好是一个完整插入过的词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: is_end is a terminal flag on a trie node; true means the path from the root to this node is exactly one complete inserted word.

q: `node.is_end = True` 在 Trie 的 `insert` 中表示什么？
q_en: What does `node.is_end = True` mean during trie insertion?
options: 把这个词从 Trie 中删除
把当前路径上所有前缀都标为非法
当前路径是一个完整词，不只是前缀
从当前节点开始一次 BFS
options_en: It deletes this word from the trie
It marks every prefix on the current path as invalid
The current path is a complete word, not just a prefix
It starts a BFS from the current node
why: 没有终止标记，`app` 和 `apple` 这类前缀关系会混淆。完整匹配必须区分“走得到”和“到达词尾”。
why_en: The terminal flag distinguishes a complete inserted word from a mere prefix path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索：按层从近到远遍历图或树的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, or Breadth-First Search, visits graph or tree nodes level by level, nearest first.

optionExplanations: 删除操作要反向清理节点，这段代码在做插入，跟删除是相反的方向。
代码里没有让 children 失效或标非法的逻辑，插入一个词不会否定其他前缀。
对，for 循环结束后打上这个标记，意思是走到这里的路径正好是一个完整词，不只是某个更长词的前缀。
BFS 是逐层遍历，这段代码是顺着 word 的字符往下插入，没有队列也没有遍历。
optionExplanations_en: Deletion would need to clean up nodes in reverse; this code is inserting, the opposite direction.
Nothing here invalidates children or other prefixes; inserting one word doesn't negate the rest.
Right — setting this after the loop means the path just walked is exactly one complete word, not merely a prefix of something longer.
BFS walks level by level with a queue; this loop just follows word's characters downward, no traversal at all.

scenario: 面试里 AI 很快写出一个逐字符生成子节点的朴素 Trie，题目要求处理大量词条并关心内存和速度。
scenario_en: In an interview, AI quickly writes a naive character-by-character trie, but the problem has many words and cares about memory and speed.
q: 朴素 Trie 在性能上可能有什么问题，应该如何缓解？
q_en: What performance issue can a naive trie have, and how can you mitigate it?
options: 朴素 Trie 在结构上完全无法表示任何字符串内容
朴素 Trie 一定比暴力搜索慢很多，应当直接放弃
朴素 Trie 完全无法支持任何前缀查询功能
换数组存 children 或用 radix trie，省内存
options_en: A naive trie structurally cannot represent any string content at all
A naive trie is always much slower than brute force and should be abandoned outright
A naive trie cannot support any prefix-query functionality at all
Switch to array-based children or a radix trie to save memory
why: AI 能很快写出正确朴素 Trie，代价是内存和指针开销；用数组代替字典存 children，或把单子节点链压缩成 radix trie，能减少节点数和跳转次数。面试中先说清是否真的需要这层优化。
why_en: A naive trie can be correct but memory- and pointer-heavy, so array-based children or a radix trie collapse reduce that overhead when performance matters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把只有单一子节点的链路压缩合并的 Trie 变体，减少节点数量和指针跳转。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A radix trie is a trie variant that collapses chains of single-child nodes to cut node count and pointer chasing.

optionExplanations: 朴素 Trie 完全能表示字符串内容，节点和路径本来就是按字符组织的，这个说法直接错了。
词表足够大时 Trie 通常比逐个比较更快，一定更慢这个断言本身站不住。
前缀查询正是 Trie 的强项，走到前缀节点就能枚举后续，这个说法否定了它的核心用途。
对，代价主要是内存里到处是指针；把 children 换成数组，或用 radix trie 合并单链节点，就能省下来。
optionExplanations_en: A naive trie fully represents string content since nodes and paths are literally organized by character; this claim is simply wrong.
With a large enough vocabulary a trie usually beats one-by-one comparison, so 'always slower' doesn't hold up.
Prefix queries are exactly what a trie is good at; walking to a prefix node and enumerating the rest is its core use.
Right — the cost shows up as extra pointers and per-node memory; swap in an array for storage or fold single-child chains into a radix layout to cut both.

scenario: 题目要求验证一个格式，处理过程有明显阶段，例如整数部分、小数点、小数部分，或引号内/引号外。
scenario_en: The task is to validate a format with clear phases, such as integer part, decimal point, decimal part, or inside versus outside quotes.
q: 应该优先考虑什么建模？
q_en: What modeling approach should you consider first?
options: 有限状态机
并查集合并连通分量
最小堆求第 K 大
只用最大硬币贪心
options_en: A finite state machine
Union-Find merging connected components
A min-heap for the Kth largest element
A greedy largest-coin-first approach
why: 当你需要追踪“当前处于格式的哪个阶段”，状态机很自然。代码只是状态和转移表的机械翻译。
why_en: A finite state machine fits validation tasks with distinct modes or phases.
whenOtherWins: 如果格式是简单平面字段抽取，regex 可能更快；如果有嵌套结构，可能需要栈或真正 parser。
tradeoff: 显式跟踪阶段状态 vs 平面正则或贪心的无状态假设

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组状态加上按输入字符触发的转移，只有落在接受状态才算合法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finite state machine is a set of states with input-driven transitions that is valid only if it ends in an accepting state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持合并集合、查询两个元素是否属于同一集合的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Disjoint Set Union supports merging sets and checking whether two elements belong to the same set.

optionExplanations: 对，格式验证要跟踪走到了哪个阶段时，用状态和转移表建模最直白，实现起来就是查表判断。
Union-Find 管的是集合合并和连通性查询，答不出当前处于格式哪个阶段这种问题。
最小堆求第 K 大是排序统计问题，跟格式有没有阶段完全没关系。
贪心默认每步独立最优，会漏掉需要记住之前阶段才能判断的情况，比如小数点后面还得看是不是数字。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when you need to track which phase the format is currently in, an FSM is the natural fit, and the code is just a mechanical translation of states and transitions.
Union-Find handles merging sets and checking connectivity, which can't answer 'which phase is the format in right now'.
A min-heap for the Kth largest is an order-statistic problem, unrelated to whether a format has phases.
Greedy assumes each step is independently optimal, so it misses cases that depend on the prior phase, like whether a digit follows the decimal point.

q: 填空：有限状态机由什么组成？
q_en: Fill in the blanks: what makes up a finite state machine?
text: FSM 由一组{{状态}}、基于输入字符的{{转移}}、以及一个或多个{{接受状态}}组成。
why: 读完整个输入后停在接受状态，字符串才合法。遇到未知转移时应进入 invalid 或返回 false。
why_en: An FSM consists of states, input-driven transitions, and accepting states.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> START
  START --> INT: digit
  INT --> INT: digit
  INT --> DOT: dot
  DOT --> DECIMAL: digit
  DECIMAL --> DECIMAL: digit
  START --> INVALID: other
  DOT --> INVALID: other

termDefinitions.meaning: 有限状态机：状态、转移和接受状态的集合，用来判断输入是否合法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An FSM, or Finite State Machine, is a collection of states, transitions, and accepting states used to judge whether input is valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入处理完毕后，只有停在这类状态，字符串才被判定为合法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An accepting state is where processing must end for the input to be judged valid.

scenario: 你在写一个小数格式验证器：读完整个字符串后，只有真正停在“已读到小数部分”这个状态，才算合法小数。
scenario_en: You are writing a decimal-format validator: after reading the whole string, it is valid only if it ends in the decimal-digits state.
q: 这个小数验证器最后为什么要 `return state == State.DECIMAL`？
q_en: Why should this decimal validator end with `return state == State.DECIMAL`?
options: 任何状态都算合法，这行判断只是保险
只有 DECIMAL 是接受状态，没崩溃不算合法
只要循环没有崩溃就应该判定为合法
DOT 状态就代表一个完整合法的小数
options_en: Any ending state counts as valid, this line is just a safety net
Only DECIMAL is the accepting state; not crashing doesn't mean it's valid
As long as the loop never raises an exception, the string should be valid
The DOT state alone already represents a complete valid decimal
why: 状态机的合法性取决于最终状态，不只是过程中没出错。比如 `12.` 到 DOT 但没有小数位，不应被接受。
why_en: FSM validation depends on ending in an accepting state, not merely avoiding invalid transitions.
optionExplanations: 代码只检查了终止状态是不是 DECIMAL，并不是任何能走到的状态都算数，这个说法夸大了。
对，只有停在 DECIMAL 才算合法小数，比如 12. 会停在 DOT，中途没崩溃不代表它是合法数字。
代码检查的是具体的终止状态，不是有没有抛异常，没崩溃就合法混淆了这两件事。
DOT 只表示刚读完小数点，还没读到任何小数位，把它当成完整小数会漏判 12. 这种非法输入。
optionExplanations_en: The code only checks whether the final state is DECIMAL, not that any reachable state passes; this overstates it.
Right — only ending in DECIMAL counts as a valid decimal; '12.' lands in DOT, and surviving the loop without crashing doesn't make it valid.
This code branches on which exact state it lands in, not on whether anything threw; equating 'no crash' with 'valid' is the mix-up.
DOT just means the decimal point was read with no digits after it yet; treating it as complete would wrongly accept '12.'.

q: 哪些问题常是状态机的伪装？
q_en: Which problems are often state machines in disguise?
options: CSV 解析，区分引号内外
IP 地址或小数格式验证
简化 glob 通配符匹配
在线连通分量合并
options_en: CSV parsing that must track inside-quotes vs outside-quotes
IP address or decimal-number format validation
Simplified glob wildcard matching
Online merging of connected components
why: 前三个都需要根据当前位置和历史模式决定下一步。在线连通分量是 Union-Find。
why_en: CSV parsing, numeric validation, and simplified glob matching all involve mode-dependent transitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以逗号分隔字段的文本表格格式，引号内的逗号不作为分隔符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CSV, Comma-Separated Values, is a text table format where commas inside quotes are not treated as separators.

termDefinitions.meaning: 此处指 IP 地址，例如 IPv4 的 a.b.c.d 数字加点格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP here refers to an IP address, such as the dotted-number IPv4 format a.b.c.d.

termDefinitions.meaning: shell 风格的通配符匹配模式，例如 `*` 匹配任意字符序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Glob is a shell-style wildcard pattern where, for example, * matches any sequence of characters.

optionExplanations: 对，引号内外是两个明确的模式，逗号在引号内不该被当成分隔符，这靠状态跟踪。
对，整数部分/小数点/小数部分是三个顺序固定的阶段，天然对应状态机。
对，`*`/`?` 这类通配符匹配要按位置记住已消耗的字符和模式，也是状态驱动的。
错，合并集合、查询是否同组是 Union-Find 的经典场景，不需要按字符阶段转移，不是状态机。
optionExplanations_en: Right — inside vs outside quotes are two explicit modes, and a comma inside quotes shouldn't act as a separator, which needs state tracking.
Right — integer part, decimal point, and decimal digits are three fixed-order phases, a natural fit for an FSM.
Right — wildcard matching like * and ? needs to track consumed characters and pattern position by mode, also state-driven.
Wrong — merging sets and checking shared membership is the classic Union-Find case; it needs no character-by-character transitions.

scenario: 每行日志都有固定平面结构：timestamp、level、message，你需要抽出这些字段。
scenario_en: Each log line has a fixed flat structure: timestamp, level, and message, and you need to extract those fields.
q: 哪种工具通常最直接？
q_en: Which tool is usually the most direct fit?
options: Dijkstra 最短路径
并查集合并连通分量
Regex，最好用命名分组
两个堆维护中位数
options_en: Dijkstra's shortest path
Union-Find merging connected components
Regex, ideally with named groups
Two heaps tracking a running median
why: Regex 很适合从平面、明确的文本结构里提取字段。命名分组比密集位置分组更可读、更好调试。
why_en: Regex is a direct tool for extracting fields from flat, well-defined text formats.
whenOtherWins: 如果日志跨多行或需要记住上下文，要在 regex 外层加状态机或解析层。
tradeoff: 平面字段抽取用 regex vs 引入和本题无关的图/堆结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 正则里给捕获组起名字（如 `(?P<level>...)`），比数字位置分组更可读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A named group gives a regex capture a label like (?P<level>...), which reads more clearly than positional groups.

optionExplanations: Dijkstra 求的是图上最短路径，跟从一行日志里抠出 timestamp/level/message 没关系。
Union-Find 管集合合并和连通性，答不出这一行的某个片段是什么字段这种问题。
对，日志是平面固定结构，一次 regex 加命名分组就能抓出三个字段，还比数字位置分组好读好调。
两个堆维护的是动态中位数，跟从一行文本里提取字段完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Dijkstra finds shortest paths in a graph, unrelated to pulling timestamp, level, and message out of one log line.
Union-Find handles merging sets and connectivity, which can't answer 'what field is this chunk of the line'.
Right — the log line is flat and fixed, so one regex with named groups grabs all three fields and reads better than positional groups.
Two heaps track a running median statistic, unrelated to pulling structured fields out of a single line.

q: Regex 适合和不适合处理什么结构？边界在哪里？
q_en: Where is the boundary between good and bad regex use in parsing?
options: 适合任何括号嵌套解析场景
只能用于纯数字字符串场景
完全不能用于日志文本场景
适合平面字段抽取，不适合嵌套或跨匹配状态
options_en: Good for parsing any level of bracket nesting
Only usable on strings that are purely digits
Cannot be used on log text at all
Good for flat field extraction; not for nested structures or state carried across matches
why: 正则在单行平面模式上高效，但平衡括号、嵌套标签、多行上下文通常需要状态机、栈或 parser。
why_en: Regex is good for flat extraction but weak for nested structures or stateful multi-line parsing.
tradeoff: 单行平面匹配的简洁 vs 嵌套/跨行状态的表达力不足
optionExplanations: 正则理论上表达不了任意深度的括号嵌套，把它的能力夸大到这个程度会在真实括号解析里翻车。
正则能处理任意文本字段，不只是数字，这个说法把它的适用范围错误地收窄了。
regex 恰恰是日志这种平面字段抽取最常用的工具，完全不能用这个说法直接否定了它最擅长的场景。
对，同一行内的平面字段正则处理得又快又准，但要跨行记住状态或处理嵌套时，得换成状态机、栈或专门写的 parser。
optionExplanations_en: Regex theoretically can't express arbitrary-depth bracket nesting; overstating this leads to real breakage on nested parsing.
Regex handles any text field, not just digits; this wrongly narrows its actual scope.
Regex is exactly the go-to tool for flat log field extraction; claiming it 'can't be used at all' denies its best use case.
Right — regex is efficient on flat single-line patterns, but nesting or state carried across lines calls for an FSM, stack, or real parser.

scenario: 你让 AI 写日志解析 regex，之前用的是数字位置分组 `(\d{4}...)(\w+)(.+)`，希望输出更可维护。
scenario_en: You asked AI to write a log-parsing regex; the previous version used numeric positional groups like `(\d{4}...)(\w+)(.+)`, and you want it to be more maintainable.
q: 相比只用数字 group，哪项改进更符合工程实践？
q_en: Compared with numeric-only groups, what improvement is more maintainable?
options: 用命名分组标出这三个字段
把所有内容写成一个未命名的贪婪 `.*`
删除对不匹配行的错误处理逻辑
改用堆结构保存所有 match 对象
options_en: Use named groups to label these three fields
Collapse everything into one unnamed greedy .* group
Remove the error handling for lines that don't match
Store every match object in a heap structure instead
why: 命名分组让字段含义直接体现在代码里。面试中可维护性比炫技式短正则更重要。
why_en: Named regex groups make extracted fields self-documenting and easier to debug.
whenOtherWins: 极短一次性脚本可以用位置分组，但面试里命名分组更能展示工程判断。
tradeoff: 命名分组的可读性 vs 位置分组的简短

termDefinitions.meaning: 正则表达式里带名字的捕获组，如 `(?P<level>\w+)`，取值时用字段名而不是数字位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A named group is a labeled regex capture, like (?P<level>\w+), accessed by field name instead of a positional index.

optionExplanations: 对，给每个捕获组标个字段名，match.group('level') 一看就懂，六个月后回来看也不用数位置。
退回到一个大大的贪婪匹配等于放弃了分组结构，之后取字段只能靠数位置，可维护性反而更差。
去掉对不匹配行的处理是牺牲健壮性，跟这里问的可维护性改进是两码事。
match 对象没有需要排序或取极值的场景，堆结构在这里纯属多余。
optionExplanations_en: Right — labeling each capture with a field name makes match.group('level') self-explanatory, no need to count positions six months later.
Collapsing back to one big greedy match throws away the grouping, so future field access falls back to counting positions, worse not better.
Dropping the handling for non-matching lines trades away robustness, a different problem from the maintainability improvement asked here.
Match objects have nothing to rank or compare, so storing them in a heap adds nothing useful here.

q: AI 生成了很聪明但很密集的 regex，你看不懂它具体在匹配什么。最佳处理是什么？
q_en: AI generated a clever but dense regex you cannot explain. What should you do?
options: 无条件接受并直接提交上线
要求 AI 简化、拆分命名分组并补测试
删除所有测试以免暴露它可能失败
改成拓扑排序处理这段文本
options_en: Accept it unconditionally and submit as-is
Ask the AI to simplify it into named groups and add tests
Delete all the tests so it can't be shown to fail
Rewrite this text processing as a topological sort instead
why: 你需要能解释和维护 regex。看不懂的模式在面试中很难 defend，也难以定位贪婪匹配或边界问题。
why_en: If an AI regex is too dense to explain, simplify it into readable named groups and test edge cases.
optionExplanations: 对看不懂的代码照单全收，等于放弃了审查责任，面试官一追问细节就答不上来。
对，把密集正则拆成可读的命名分组，再用对抗输入验证边界，既解决了可读性也补上了验证。
删测试只是把问题藏起来而不是解决，风险反而更高。
拓扑排序跟文本匹配没关系，换个不相关的算法答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Accepting code you can't explain gives up review responsibility, and you'll freeze the moment the interviewer asks about details.
Right — turn the tangle into groups you can name and explain, then throw multi-tag and empty-input cases at it to be sure.
Deleting the tests just hides the problem instead of fixing it, which raises the risk.
Topological sort has nothing to do with text matching, so swapping it in doesn't address the question.

scenario: 题目要求解析任意层嵌套的括号或标签，比如 `((a)(b(c)))` 这样的结构。
scenario_en: The task asks you to parse arbitrarily nested parentheses or tags, such as `((a)(b(c)))`.
q: 为什么不应只靠普通 regex？
q_en: Why should you not rely only on ordinary regex here?
options: regex 理论上不能匹配任何字符
栈这种结构只能用于图搜索问题
嵌套结构需要栈记住深度，regex 没有递归状态
嵌套结构一定要靠 LRU 缓存解决
options_en: Regex theoretically cannot match any characters at all
A stack can only be used for graph-search problems
Nested structures need a stack to remember depth; regex has no recursive state
Nested structures must be solved with an LRU cache
why: 平衡结构需要记住未闭合的层级。状态机或栈式 parser 比单个正则更符合问题结构。
why_en: Nested balanced structures need stack-like parsing state rather than a plain regex.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一层固定格式，regex 仍然可能足够。
tradeoff: 栈式 parser 的递归深度记忆 vs 正则的无状态平面匹配

termDefinitions.meaning: 后进先出的数据结构，常用来记录未闭合的嵌套层级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stack is a last-in-first-out structure often used to track unclosed nesting levels.

optionExplanations: 正则能匹配任意字符类，只是没有办法记住嵌套深度，说它匹配不了任何字符是描述错误。
栈在表达式和括号解析里同样常见，把它的用途收窄到只有图搜索是错的。
对，栈记住还没闭合的括号/标签层级，遇到闭括号就出栈匹配，能处理任意嵌套深度，这正是正则做不到的。
LRU 解决的是缓存淘汰问题，完全不追踪嵌套深度，判断不了括号是否平衡。
optionExplanations_en: Regex can match any character class fine; it just can't remember nesting depth, so 'can't match any characters' mischaracterizes it.
Stacks are just as common in expression and bracket parsing, so narrowing them to graph search only is wrong.
Right — a stack remembers unclosed bracket/tag levels and pops on each close, handling any nesting depth, exactly what plain regex can't do.
LRU solves cache eviction and tracks nothing about nesting depth, so it can't judge whether brackets balance.

q: 一个真实日志分析器可能组合哪些层？
q_en: What layers might a real log analyzer combine?
options: 状态机处理多行日志条目边界
Regex 从单行中抽 timestamp、level、message
Trie 或表查找把错误码归类到已知签名
两个堆计算滚动中位数
options_en: A state machine handling multi-line log-entry boundaries
Regex extracting timestamp, level, and message from each line
A trie or table lookup classifying error codes against known signatures
Two heaps computing a rolling median
why: 字符串题常需要组合工具，而不是单一技巧。关键是把每层单独测试后再组装。
why_en: Real string-processing tasks often combine state machines, regex extraction, and trie or table classification.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw log text] --> Records[Record boundaries]
  Records --> Regex[Extract fields]
  Regex --> Classify[Classify known signatures]
  Classify --> Aggregate[Aggregate results]
optionExplanations: 对，判断多行是不是属于同一个逻辑日志条目要靠状态机跨行记状态。
对，从每行结构化文本里切字段，用 regex 是标准做法。
对，把抽出的错误码和已知签名集合比对做分类，Trie 或表查找是候选。
错，滚动中位数这种统计量跟日志分析器要分的层完全没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right — telling whether several lines form one logical record is exactly the multi-line tracking an FSM is built for.
Right — slicing each structured line into fields is the standard job for regex.
Right — matching an error code against a known signature set is a lookup problem, which a prefix tree or table check handles well.
Wrong — a rolling median statistic has nothing to do with the layers a log analyzer needs.

q: 把日志分析器的分层设计按合理顺序排列。
q_en: Put the log analyzer layers in a reasonable order.
steps: 把抽出的错误码或消息模式交给 Trie/表做分类。
先确定日志记录边界，必要时用状态机处理多行条目。
对每层写小测试，再组合成完整流水线。
用 regex 从单条记录里抽结构化字段。
聚合统计或输出最终结果。
why: 先切记录，再抽字段，再分类和聚合。每层独立验证，能避免最后面对一坨混合 bug。
why_en: A layered parser first finds record boundaries, extracts fields, classifies them, aggregates results, and tests each layer.
tradeoff: 分层顺序推进 vs 一次性写完整个流水线
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Raw log line] --> B[Regex tokenize]
B --> C[State machine validate]
C --> D[Normalize fields]
D --> E[Aggregate results]

scenario: 你要实现一个包含抽取、分类和聚合的日志工具，正在决定怎么向 AI 分批下达指令。
scenario_en: You need to build a log tool with extraction, classification, and aggregation, and you are deciding how to prompt AI in batches.
q: 怎样提示 AI 最稳？
q_en: What is the most stable way to prompt the AI?
options: 一个 prompt 里要求所有功能且不写测试
让 AI 随机决定日志格式的细节规则
先写聚合逻辑，忽略解析层是否正确
一次只让 AI 写一层，例如先写单行 regex
options_en: Ask for every feature in one prompt with no tests
Let the AI randomly decide the log format's detail rules
Write the aggregation logic first and ignore whether parsing is correct
Prompt one layer at a time, like the single-line regex first
why: 分层提示能让每个组件独立可测。一次生成大块代码会把 regex、状态和聚合错误混在一起，难以定位。
why_en: Prompting one layer at a time keeps string-processing code testable and debuggable.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务只有一个很小的固定解析步骤，一次提示即可；复杂流水线应拆分。
tradeoff: 分层提示便于定位 bug vs 一次性提示看起来更快
optionExplanations: 把抽取、分类、聚合一股脑塞进一个 prompt，出错时根本分不清是哪一层的问题。
格式定义该是你来把关的判断，交给 AI 随机决定只会产出不一致的解析规则。
先写聚合、不确认上游解析对不对，等于把错误建立在没验证的数据上，还会被放大。
对，一次只描述一层的输入输出、验证过再进下一层，出错时能马上定位到具体哪一层。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming extraction, classification, and aggregation into one prompt leaves no way to tell which layer broke when it fails.
Format definition should be your call; letting the AI decide randomly produces inconsistent parsing rules.
Writing aggregation first without confirming upstream parsing builds on unverified data, and errors compound.
Right — describe one layer's input and output at a time, verify it, then move on, so a failure points straight at that layer.

q: 字符串题中，哪些提示习惯有帮助？
q_en: Which prompting habits help on string problems?
options: Regex：用自然语言描述匹配内容并要求命名分组
FSM：先列出状态和转移，再让 AI 翻译成代码
Trie：结构标准，可以直接要求实现，但重点说明如何使用它
所有层混在一起，让 AI 自己猜边界
options_en: Regex: describe the match in plain English and ask for named groups
FSM: list states and transitions first, then let the AI translate them to code
Trie: the structure is standard, ask for it directly but focus on how it's used
Mix every layer together and let the AI guess the boundaries
why: 每种工具的提示重点不同。共同点是把人类的结构判断讲清，让 AI 做机械实现。
why_en: Good string prompts tailor the instruction to the tool: named groups for regex, state sketches for FSMs, and usage context for tries.
optionExplanations: 对，先讲清要匹配什么，再要求命名分组，抽出的字段自带文档。
对，先列状态和转移表，代码就只是照着表机械翻译。
对，Trie 实现套路固定，真正该讲清楚的是它怎么接进整个系统。
错，把结构判断这个人该做的活也丢给 AI 猜，边界会猜得不一致。
optionExplanations_en: Right — say what you're matching in plain words, then require named captures so the extracted fields explain themselves.
Right — list the states and transitions first, and the code becomes a mechanical translation of that table.
Right — a trie's implementation is standard, so the real thing to clarify is how it plugs into the system.
Wrong — leaving the structural judgment for the AI to guess produces inconsistent boundaries.

q: AI 字符串处理代码常见的失败模式有哪些？
q_en: What are common failure modes in AI-generated string code?
options: 位置跟踪 off-by-one
缺少异常/畸形输入处理
Regex 贪婪匹配吃掉太多内容
结构边界，如空串、单字符、前后空白、最大长度
options_en: Off-by-one errors in position tracking
Missing handling for malformed or unexpected input
Greedy regex matching that consumes too much
Structural boundaries like empty strings, single characters, leading or trailing whitespace, max length
why: 字符串 bug 往往藏在 consume/advance、未知字符、贪婪量词和边界输入里。测试要专门覆盖这些点。
why_en: String bugs often involve off-by-one consumption, malformed inputs, greedy regex, and boundary cases.
optionExplanations: 位置计数多算或少算一格，常在窗口滑动或状态机转移时冒出来，容易漏测。
没处理的畸形输入会让代码在真实脏数据前直接崩溃或悄悄给出错误结果。
`.*` 默认尽量多吃字符，多标签或嵌套输入下会一路吃过头，需要专门测试。
空串、单字符、首尾空白这些边界不会出现在 happy path 样例里，最容易被漏测。
optionExplanations_en: Off-by-one index errors sneak in during window sliding or FSM transitions and are easy to miss testing.
Skipping this means the code breaks or silently misfires the moment real-world messy data shows up.
.* greedily consumes as much as it can, overmatching on multi-tag or nested input unless you test for it.
Empty strings, single characters, and leading/trailing whitespace never show up in happy-path examples, easiest to skip.

scenario: 输入总是简单的 `key=value` 行，只需要按第一个等号拆成两部分，值本身可能也含有等号。
scenario_en: The input is always a simple `key=value` line; split only on the first equals sign because the value may also contain equals signs.
q: 最合适的工具是什么？
q_en: What is the best-fitting tool?
options: `split('=', 1)` 这样的简单字符串操作
为这行写一个复杂的 regex
引入完整 parser generator
用 Dijkstra 处理这一行文本
options_en: A simple string operation like split('=', 1)
Write a complex regex for this one line
Bring in a full parser generator
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to process this line
why: 固定简单格式用 split 更清晰、更少 bug。过度使用重工具在面试中是校准不佳的信号。maxsplit=1 保证只在第一个等号处拆分，值里的等号不会被误切。
why_en: For simple fixed key-value lines, split is clearer and safer than regex.
whenOtherWins: 如果字段格式更复杂、需要可选字段或严格验证，regex 或状态机可能更合适。
tradeoff: split 的简单直接 vs regex/parser 的重量级但灵活

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据语法规则自动生成解析代码的工具，适合复杂嵌套语言而非一行固定格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parser generator automatically produces parsing code from grammar rules, suited to complex nested languages rather than one fixed-format line.

optionExplanations: 对，一行 split('=', 1) 就搞定，第二个参数限制只切一次，保证值里的等号原样留着。
为一个固定分隔符写正则能做到同样的事，但多了写和调正则的成本，没必要。
为一行固定格式的 key=value 引入完整语法解析框架，学习和维护成本远超这个任务本身。
Dijkstra 是图上最短路径算法，跟按分隔符拆一行字符串完全不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right — split('=', 1) does it in one line, and maxsplit=1 splits only at the first equals sign, so one inside the value stays intact.
A regex could do the same job, but it adds the cost of writing and debugging a pattern for one fixed separator.
A full grammar-parsing framework for one fixed key=value line costs far more to learn and maintain than the task justifies.
Dijkstra is a shortest-path algorithm on graphs, unrelated to splitting one line on a separator.

q: Regex 和状态机在字符串解析里的分界线是什么？
q_en: Where is the boundary between regex and state machines in string parsing?
options: 状态机只能验证纯数字格式
Regex 适合平面模式；状态机适合跟踪模式阶段
Regex 总能处理任意上下文相关的语法
二者的适用场景之间完全没有重叠
options_en: A state machine can only validate pure digit formats
Regex fits flat patterns; an FSM fits tracking phase or mode
Regex can always handle arbitrary context-sensitive grammar
Their use cases have zero overlap with each other
why: 一旦你需要知道“我现在在引号里还是外面”，状态变量就比单个正则更清晰。平面字段抽取则 regex 更快。
why_en: Regex is best for flat patterns, while FSMs are best when the parser must track modes.
tradeoff: 无状态的平面正则匹配 vs 有状态的阶段/模式跟踪
optionExplanations: 状态机同样适用于引号内外、glob 这类非数字场景，把它收窄到只有数字格式是错的。
对，平面单行抽字段用 regex 更快，一旦要跟踪现在处于哪个阶段就该换状态机。
正则理论上表达不了上下文相关语法，把它的能力夸大到这个地步会在真实场景里翻车。
简单格式两者其实都能覆盖，只是复杂度不同，说零重叠否认了这块交集。
optionExplanations_en: FSMs apply just as well to non-digit cases like tracking inside/outside quotes or glob patterns; narrowing them to digits only is wrong.
Right — regex is faster for flat single-line extraction, but once you need to track 'which phase am I in', switch to an FSM.
Regex fundamentally can't express context-sensitive grammar; overstating its power this way breaks on real cases.
Simple formats can actually be handled by either tool, just at different complexity, so 'zero overlap' denies that overlap zone.

scenario: 每行日志都要和数千个固定错误签名比对，重复跑数千个 regex 太慢。
scenario_en: Each log line must be checked against thousands of fixed error signatures, and running thousands of regexes repeatedly is too slow.
q: 更合理的结构方向是什么？
q_en: What structure direction is more reasonable?
options: 继续逐个签名跑 regex 暴力比对
用最小堆对日志排序后再比对
把固定签名预编译进 Trie 或相关多模式结构
先做拓扑排序再比对
options_en: Keep testing each signature one by one with regex
Sort the logs with a min-heap before comparing
Precompile the fixed signatures into a trie or similar multi-pattern structure
Run a topological sort before comparing
why: 固定模式集合可以预处理成共享前缀结构，查询时不用对每个 pattern 单独扫描。文章用 Trie 代表这种预编译思路。
why_en: Many fixed patterns should be precompiled into a trie-like structure instead of tested one by one.
whenOtherWins: 如果 pattern 很少或格式复杂到不是固定字符串，简单 regex 列表可能更直接。
tradeoff: 一次预编译、多次快速查询 vs 每次查询都重新扫描全部签名
optionExplanations: 对每行都跑一遍全部签名的正则，正是题目说的太慢的做法，签名越多线性变慢。
排序解决的是日志先后顺序，不判断某行是否命中已知签名，答非所问。
对，把数千个固定签名一次性编译成共享前缀的 Trie，查询复杂度只跟字符串长度有关，不再随签名数量线性增长。
拓扑排序解决的是依赖顺序问题，跟这行是否匹配已知签名完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Running every signature's regex against every log line is exactly the 'too slow' approach described here; it grows linearly with signature count.
Sorting only reorders the logs; it can't determine whether a line matches a known signature.
Right — precompile thousands of fixed signatures into a shared-prefix trie once, so each query scales with string length, not signature count.
Topological sort addresses dependency order, unrelated to whether a line matches a known signature.

q: 字符串解析题中，应主动测试哪些畸形或边界输入？
q_en: Which malformed or boundary inputs should you test in string parsing?
options: 空字符串
缺字段或部分匹配
意外字符
前后空白或单字符输入
options_en: Empty string
Missing fields or a partial match
Unexpected characters
Leading/trailing whitespace or single-character input
why: happy path 通常会过，畸形输入才暴露错误处理和状态转移缺口。面试中明确这些测试是强信号。
why_en: Malformed and boundary inputs expose parser behavior that happy-path examples rarely cover.
optionExplanations: 空字符串最容易让索引越界或死循环，是最基础的边界检查。
只写一半的格式该被明确拒绝，不能悄悄被判成部分成功。
状态机或正则遇到没预料到的字符时，要有明确的失败路径而不是沉默通过。
首尾空白和单字符输入常被 happy path 样例忽略，容易漏测。
optionExplanations_en: Empty strings are the most basic boundary check; they easily trigger index errors or infinite loops.
A half-written format should be explicitly rejected, not silently treated as a partial success.
When an FSM or regex hits an unexpected character, it needs an explicit failure path instead of silently passing.
Padding and single-character inputs sit right at the edge that clean sample inputs never touch.

scenario: AI 写的 regex 用了贪婪 `.*`，标签之间有多个 `<tag>...</tag>` 时匹配从第一个开始标签一路吃到最后一个结束标签。
scenario_en: AI wrote a regex with greedy `.*`, so with multiple `<tag>...</tag>` blocks it matches from the first opening tag to the last closing tag.
q: 合理修正是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable fix?
options: 直接删除结束标签的匹配部分
改用 Dijkstra 求最短匹配范围
改用非贪婪 `.*?` 或更窄字符类，并测多标签
options_en: Simply remove the closing-tag part of the pattern
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest matching span
Change .* into an even longer .*.*
Switch to a lazy .*? or a narrower character class, and test multi-tag input
why: 贪婪量词会尽可能多吃字符。非贪婪或更具体字符类能限制匹配范围，但仍要用对抗输入验证。
why_en: Greedy dot-star can overmatch, so use a lazy quantifier or a specific character class and test adversarial cases.
whenOtherWins: 如果标签可嵌套，正则修补仍不够，应使用栈式 parser。
tradeoff: 非贪婪/更窄字符类的精确匹配 vs 贪婪 `.*` 的简单但过度吞噬

termDefinitions.meaning: 正则里 `*`/`+` 默认尽量多匹配字符的行为，如 `.*` 会吃到最后一个可能的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy quantifier is the default regex behavior of matching as many characters as possible, so .* extends to the last possible position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在量词后加 `?`（如 `.*?`），让它尽量少匹配字符，匹配到第一个满足条件的位置就停止。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lazy quantifier, written with a trailing ? like .*?, matches as few characters as possible, stopping at the first valid point.

optionExplanations: 去掉结束标签的匹配，等于连必须成对出现这个基本约束都不检查了，问题只会更严重。
最短路径算法不是正则引擎的匹配机制，用错了工具类别，答非所问。
把 .* 再叠一个 .*，本质还是贪婪，问题一点没解决，反而更难读。
对，改成非贪婪 .*? 或用 [^<]* 排除标签字符，能让匹配停在最近的结束标签，再用多标签输入验证。
optionExplanations_en: Removing the closing-tag match drops even the basic 'must be paired' constraint, making it worse, not better.
Shortest-path algorithms aren't part of how a regex engine matches; this is the wrong category of tool entirely.
Stacking another .* is still greedy underneath; nothing is fixed and it's harder to read.
Right — switch to a lazy .*? or [^<]* to exclude tag characters so the match stops at the nearest closing tag, then verify with multi-tag input.

q: 把字符串处理流水线的验证顺序排好。
q_en: Put the string-processing validation steps in order.
steps: 加入状态机包装后，用小型多行输入测试记录边界。
最后组合并测试聚合结果。
先用三四个单行输入测试 regex 或 split。
加入 Trie/分类层后，用已知和未知签名测试。
对空输入、部分匹配和特殊字符补边界测试。
why: 每层先单独证明，再组合。边界测试可以穿插做，但最终必须覆盖整条流水线。
why_en: Incremental string validation tests extraction, state wrapping, classification, aggregation, and then malformed boundaries.
tradeoff: 逐层增量验证 vs 攒到最后一次性测试整条流水线
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Unit1[Test record split] --> Unit2[Test field regex]
  Unit2 --> Unit3[Test classifier]
  Unit3 --> Whole[Test full pipeline]
  Whole --> Edge[Test malformed input]

q: 字符串解析题里，面试官最想看到的强信号是什么？
q_en: What is the strongest interview signal in a string parsing problem?
options: 先分解层次，再为每层选择合适工具并独立测试
一上来就写一个巨大的单体 regex
拒绝处理畸形输入，只覆盖 happy path
让 AI 猜完整架构再一次性接受
options_en: Decompose into layers first, pick the right tool per layer, and test each independently
Jump straight into one giant monolithic regex
Refuse to handle malformed input and only cover the happy path
Let the AI guess the whole architecture and accept it in one shot
why: 字符串题模拟真实工程任务，分解能力比炫技更重要。每层可测，最后组合才稳。
why_en: Strong string-parsing answers decompose the task, pick the right tool per layer, and test each layer independently.
optionExplanations: 对，先说清哪层用什么工具，再逐层实现和验证，出错时能立刻定位到具体哪一层。
一上来就堆一个巨大正则，出了问题很难调试，也很难向面试官解释匹配逻辑。
只覆盖 happy path 上线后遇到真实脏数据容易翻车，也让人怀疑工程严谨性。
把架构判断这个该你做的工作外包给 AI 又不审查，面试官看不到你的技术判断。
optionExplanations_en: Right — say which tool fits which layer first, then implement and verify layer by layer, so a failure points straight at that layer.
Jumping straight to one giant regex makes it hard to debug when it breaks and hard to explain the logic to an interviewer.
Covering only the happy path breaks the moment real dirty data shows up, and signals weak engineering rigor.
Outsourcing the architecture judgment call to the AI without reviewing it means the interviewer never sees your technical thinking.

q: 为什么“用最重的工具”不是字符串题的好策略？
q_en: Why is using the heaviest tool a poor strategy for string problems?
options: 重工具在字符串题里一定无法运行
过度设计增加 bug 面和解释成本，看工具匹配度
简单工具在任何情况下都是错误答案
AI 写不出复杂的 regex 模式
options_en: Heavy tools simply cannot run on string problems
Overengineering adds bug surface and explaining cost; it's about tool fit
A simple tool is always the wrong answer in every case
AI cannot write a complex regex pattern
why: key=value 用 split，平面抽字段用 regex，有模式状态才用 FSM。工具越贴合，越容易验证和解释。
why_en: String tasks reward calibration: the simplest tool that matches the structure is usually best.
tradeoff: 工具复杂度匹配问题结构 vs 无脑上重型工具显得“更专业”
optionExplanations: 重工具通常能跑起来，只是没必要，说它一定无法运行是夸大了后果。
对，重工具会带来更多代码面、更难解释也更难维护，问题不在能不能跑，而在跟结构合不合适。
简单工具在匹配简单结构时恰恰是最优解，把它极端化成任何情况都错忽略了这个前提。
AI 完全能写出复杂正则，这也正是它更该被审查的原因，不是它写不出来。
optionExplanations_en: Heavy tools usually can run just fine; they're just unnecessary, so 'cannot run at all' overstates the downside.
Right — a heavier tool means more code to get wrong and more to explain; the goal is matching tool weight to problem shape.
A simple tool is exactly the right call for a simple structure, so calling it 'always wrong' ignores that condition.
AI can write complex regex just fine, which is exactly why it needs review, not because it's incapable.

q: 填空：为什么先写暴力搜索有时很有价值？
q_en: Fill in the blank: why can writing brute-force search first be valuable?
text: 朴素版本容易验证，可作为更快算法的{{参考 oracle}}，避免同时调试{{性能}}和{{正确性}}。
why: 先有一个可相信的 baseline，再优化 trie/KMP/其他结构，能让失败定位更清晰。不要一开始就把复杂度和正确性混在一起。
why_en: A brute-force baseline can serve as a reference oracle before optimizing performance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个已知正确、可用来核对更快实现是否行为一致的简单版本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference oracle is a known-correct, simple implementation used to check that a faster version behaves the same way.

scenario: 你要实现固定词表的 autocomplete，用户输入前缀后返回所有可能的补全词。
scenario_en: You need to implement autocomplete over a fixed vocabulary, returning all completions for a user-entered prefix.
q: 为什么 Trie 是合适结构？
q_en: Why is a trie the right structure?
options: 它能求带权图上的最短路
它自动解析任意嵌套括号
它共享前缀，走到前缀节点再枚举后续词
它按访问顺序维护最近使用的词
options_en: It computes shortest paths in a weighted graph
It automatically parses arbitrarily nested brackets
It shares prefixes, so you can walk to the prefix node and enumerate the rest
It tracks the most recently used words by access order
why: 自动补全的核心是前缀查询，Trie 直接把前缀路径编码进结构。走到前缀节点后再遍历子树即可枚举补全词。
why_en: A trie is well suited to autocomplete because it shares prefixes and can enumerate completions from a prefix node.
whenOtherWins: 如果词表很小，排序数组加二分范围也可能足够；需要按频率排名时还要额外维护权重。
tradeoff: 前缀共享一次遍历 vs 每次都扫描整个词表找匹配前缀
optionExplanations: Dijkstra 求的是带权图最短路径，跟这个前缀后面能接哪些词没关系。
Trie 本身不解析括号嵌套，这是把它的能力错误地类比成了另一件事。
对，共同前缀只存一份，从根走到前缀节点后，子树里的都是候选词，开销只跟前缀长度有关。
LRU 管的是最近用过谁，自动补全要的是以这个前缀开头的词，两者答的不是同一个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Dijkstra finds shortest paths in a weighted graph, unrelated to 'which words follow this prefix'.
A trie doesn't parse bracket nesting on its own; this misattributes a different capability to it.
Right — a shared prefix is stored once, so walking from root to the prefix node leaves its subtree as candidates, cost tied only to prefix length.
LRU tracks recency of access; here we need every word sharing a given prefix, a different lookup than recency.

scenario: 模板引擎只需要把 `{{name}}` 这种平面变量占位符替换成值，不允许嵌套表达式或条件逻辑。
scenario_en: The template engine only replaces flat placeholders like `{{name}}` with values; it does not allow nested expressions or conditionals.
q: 合理起点是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable starting point?
options: 先实现一个完整编程语言解释器
用 Dijkstra 求占位符的替换顺序
用并查集合并所有占位符
Regex 或简单扫描抽变量名，再用映射替换
options_en: Implement a full programming-language interpreter first
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to order the placeholder substitutions
Use Union-Find to merge all the placeholders
Regex or a simple scan to extract variable names, then substitute via a lookup map
why: 平面占位符不需要复杂 parser，正则抓变量名、字典查值替换即可。若未来支持嵌套表达式、条件或循环，再升级到 tokenization/parser。
why_en: Flat template placeholders can be handled with regex or simple scanning before escalating to a parser.
whenOtherWins: 如果模板语言包含嵌套块、条件或表达式，应转向真正解析器或状态机。
tradeoff: 平面占位符用轻量扫描 vs 提前引入完整解释器的复杂度
optionExplanations: 为平面占位符引入完整的词法+语法分析引擎，开发和维护成本跟当前需求完全不匹配。
占位符替换互不依赖，不存在需要排序的最短路径问题，用错了工具类别。
并查集解决的是集合合并，占位符之间没有需要合并的关系，答非所问。
对，扫描找出 {{name}} 里的变量名，去映射表查值再拼回字符串，实现量小、替换顺序也不重要。
optionExplanations_en: Building a full lexer and parser for a substitution this flat costs way more than the task calls for.
Placeholder substitutions are independent, so there's no ordering problem to solve; the wrong category of tool.
Union-Find is for merging groups of elements; there's no such relationship between independent placeholders.
Right — scan for the variable name inside {{name}}, look it up in a map, and splice the value back in; small to build, order doesn't matter.

scenario: 这是一个整数验证状态机在 INTEGER 状态下的转移分支，`ch` 是当前读到的字符。
scenario_en: This is a transition branch in an integer-validation state machine while in the INTEGER state, and `ch` is the current character.
q: 状态机代码中，遇到没有定义转移的字符时应怎样处理？
q_en: In state-machine code, how should an undefined transition character be handled?
options: 进 INVALID 状态或返回 False
忽略这个字符，继续处理下一个
把它当作数字字符处理
重置回 START 状态并继续
options_en: Enter the INVALID state or return False
Ignore this character and continue with the next one
Treat it as if it were a digit character
Reset back to the START state and continue
why: 验证器必须明确处理意外输入。静默忽略未知字符会让非法字符串被错误接受。
why_en: FSM validators should reject undefined transitions instead of silently ignoring unexpected characters.
optionExplanations: 对，代码的 else 分支正是这么写的：碰到没定义的转移就直接进 INVALID，未知字符不能被放过。
跳过字符不改变状态，等于假装它不存在，会让 12x3 这种带非法字符的输入被误判合法。
把非数字字符当数字处理会污染后续状态判断，代码里 isdigit() 明明白白区分了两者。
重置回 START 会丢掉已经读到的合法前缀，跟代码实际逻辑不符，也没有这个分支。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the else clause routes any unmapped character straight to INVALID instead of letting it pass quietly.
Skipping the character without changing state is like pretending it isn't there, which would wrongly accept input like '12x3'.

q: 为什么每层都要独立测试？
q_en: Why should each layer be tested independently?
options: regex 错误能在单行样例上快速定位
状态机边界能在小型多行样例上快速定位
Trie 分类能用已知/未知词快速验证
所有层混在一起更容易定位 bug
options_en: Regex errors can be pinpointed quickly with single-line examples
State-machine boundaries can be pinpointed quickly with small multi-line examples
Trie classification can be verified quickly with known and unknown words
Mixing every layer together makes bugs easier to pinpoint
why: 分层测试能把错误停在引入它的层。混在一起只会让你不知道是抽取、状态还是分类坏了。
why_en: Layer-level tests localize whether extraction, state handling, or classification introduced a bug.
optionExplanations: 对，三四个单行输入就能确认字段抽取对不对，不牵扯其他层。
对，几行多行样例就能确认记录边界和状态转移对不对。
对，一个已知词加一个未知词就能确认分类逻辑对不对。
错，层混在一起时，一个错误结果根本没法判断是哪一层引入的。
optionExplanations_en: Right — three or four single-line inputs confirm field extraction alone, without touching other layers.
Right — a few short multi-line examples confirm record boundaries and state transitions alone.
Right — one word from the vocabulary and one outside it are enough to confirm the classifier works on its own.
Wrong — when layers are mixed, a wrong result can't be traced back to which layer caused it.

q: 在字符串题中，AI 最适合承担哪部分工作？
q_en: In string problems, what work is AI best suited for?
options: 替你决定产品格式和边界处理行为
实现 Trie、regex 草案或 FSM 骨架
跳过所有畸形或异常输入的处理
断言任何 regex 输出都天然可维护
options_en: Deciding the product format and edge-case behavior on your behalf
Implement a trie, a regex draft, or an FSM skeleton
Skipping the handling of all malformed input
Asserting that any regex is inherently maintainable
why: AI 写单层 boilerplate 很强，但格式定义、边界策略和组件连接是你要主导的部分。面试官看的是这个工程判断。
why_en: AI is strong at mechanical string-building blocks, while you should own the format, edge cases, and composition.
optionExplanations: 格式和边界策略是产品/工程判断，该由你主导，交给 AI 决定容易得到不一致的行为。
对，标准 Trie、regex 草案、FSM 骨架这类套路固定的机械层，AI 生成正确率很高，正该交给它。
畸形输入处理需要人明确要求，不该被默认跳过，否则上线遇到脏数据直接翻车。
regex 可不可维护取决于有没有用命名分组这类写法，不是天然属性，这个断言站不住。
optionExplanations_en: Format and edge-case strategy are engineering judgment calls that should stay with you; handing them to the AI risks inconsistent behavior.
Right — mechanical layers like a standard trie, a regex draft, or an FSM skeleton are formulaic, and AI gets these right most of the time.
Malformed-input handling needs an explicit human requirement, not a default skip, or real dirty data breaks it in production.
Regex maintainability depends on choices like named groups, not some inherent property; this claim doesn't hold.

q: 字符串匹配/解析题的核心工作流是什么？
q_en: What is the core workflow for string matching and parsing problems?
options: 先写一个巨型函数再祈祷它能跑
只用 regex 解决所有文本问题
识别子模式，分层提示 AI 并逐层验证组合
完全不测试边界输入
options_en: Write one giant function first and hope it works
Use regex to solve every text problem
Recognize the sub-pattern, prompt AI layer by layer, verify each, and combine
Never test boundary input at all
why: 这类题最考校准：什么时候 split 足够，什么时候 regex、FSM、Trie 更合适。正确的分层让 AI 产出更容易审查。
why_en: The string workflow is to choose the right subtools, prompt one layer at a time, and verify each layer before composition.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Signals[Read text signals] --> Split[Split into layers]
  Split --> Tool[Choose tool per layer]
  Tool --> AI[Prompt AI for one layer]
  AI --> Verify[Verify then compose]
optionExplanations: 先写一个巨型函数再祈祷，出了问题既难调试，面试时也讲不清设计思路。
把 regex 当成唯一工具，遇到嵌套结构或跨行状态就直接失效。
对，先判断需要哪些子工具，按层提示 AI 并逐层验证，最后再组合，这条主线覆盖了识别到验证的全过程。
放弃边界测试，违反了畸形输入必须验证这个强信号要求，上线遇脏数据容易翻车。
optionExplanations_en: Writing one giant function and hoping it works is hard to debug and hard to explain the design behind it in an interview.
Treating regex as the only tool breaks the moment nested structures or cross-line state show up.
Right — figure out which small tools apply, have the AI build one piece at a time, check each, and only then wire them together.
Skipping boundary tests violates the strong signal that malformed input must be verified, and it breaks on real dirty data.
